companies.name: Tapestry (Google/Alphabet)
companies.what: Alphabet's grid moonshot applying DeepMind/Google Cloud AI to grid planning and operations workflows for system operators.
companies.signal: Multiyear collaboration with PJM announced April 2025; phased tool rollout began 2025

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.what: Embedding AI/ML assistants and automation across the GridOS suite used in existing control rooms.
companies.signal: AI for grid operations a headline theme of its Orchestrate 2025 user conference

companies.name: EPRI
companies.what: Convenes the Open Power AI Consortium with NVIDIA and global utilities to build domain-specific AI models for grid operations.
companies.signal: Consortium launched 2025 with dozens of utility members

companies.name: NVIDIA

variations.white_space: Almost no credible players because control rooms are NERC-CIP-bound, safety-critical, and demand physics-verifiable recommendations — pure-LLM startups can't clear the trust bar (national labs like Argonne's GridMind are still at research stage). The opening is audited, physics-constrained copilots sold with or through EMS incumbents, mirroring ThinkLabs' GE lineage.

variations.name: Interconnection queue & hosting capacity automation

companies.name: Pearl Street Technologies

companies.signal: Deployed with MISO to automate Definitive Planning Phase studies; backed by VoLo Earth, Pear VC, Powerhouse, Incite

companies.name: Nira Energy

companies.signal: Bootstrapped to profitability in year one; later strategic investment from Energize Capital

companies.name: GridUnity
companies.what: Cloud workflow platform that manages interconnection application intake and study coordination for RTOs and utilities, including PJM's reformed cycle process.
companies.signal: $49.5M DOE award — the largest federal investment in interconnection automation to date

companies.name: Tapestry (Google/Alphabet)
companies.what: Building AI models with Google Cloud/DeepMind to accelerate PJM's generation interconnection and regional planning analysis.
companies.signal: PJM partnership announced 2025; first AI tools in limited testing

companies.name: Kevala
companies.what: Parcel-level grid analytics: hosting capacity, DER siting, and grid-impact studies built from public and utility data.
companies.signal: $21M Series A (2022); DOE-funded hosting-capacity work

companies.name: envelio

companies.signal: 60+ utilities including E.ON, Europe's largest DSO; US entity opened 2024

variations.white_space: Few players because the buyers are a handful of RTOs/ISOs and large utilities with multi-year procurement and physics-grade validation requirements; FERC itself now recommends automation. The open flank is distribution-level interconnection and hosting-capacity automation for the ~3,000 smaller utilities, plus large-load (data center) connection studies.

variations.name: Transmission planning & expansion analytics

companies.name: Energy Exemplar
companies.what: PLEXOS/Aurora co-optimized market and expansion simulation used for long-term transmission and resource planning in 79 countries.
companies.signal: Acquired by Blackstone + Vista Equity for >$1B (2023); 500+ customers, ~30% CAGR since 2018

companies.name: Siemens (PSS/E)
companies.what: PSS/E, the de facto standard transmission power-flow and dynamics simulator for planning engineers.
companies.signal: Decades-deep installed base across TSOs and utilities globally

companies.name: PowerWorld
companies.what: Interactive power system simulator widely used for planning studies, visualization, and education in North America.
companies.signal: Standard tool across US planning departments and universities

companies.name: Hitachi Energy (PROMOD/GridView)
companies.what: Production-cost and transmission congestion modeling used in RTO planning and FERC filings.
companies.signal: PROMOD remains a reference model in US transmission benefit studies

companies.name: encoord
companies.what: SAInt platform co-simulates gas and electric networks for integrated infrastructure and resilience planning.
companies.signal: Used by utilities, regulators, and NREL-linked research projects

companies.name: Vibrant Clean Energy
companies.what: WIS:dom high-resolution co-optimized capacity-expansion model that pioneered joint DER + transmission planning studies.
companies.signal: Influential MISO/state studies ~2019-2022 but little public commercial activity since — viability unconfirmed

variations.white_space: A legacy oligopoly (PSS/E, PowerWorld, PLEXOS, PROMOD) protected by decades of model validation and regulatory acceptance; AI-native challengers are only now arriving via Tapestry/PJM. FERC Order 1920 long-term scenario planning plus data-center load growth create demand for orders-of-magnitude faster co-optimization that none of the legacy tools deliver.

variations.name: Grid-enhancing technology software (dynamic line ratings, topology optimization, congestion management)

companies.name: LineVision

companies.signal: Series B led by UP Partners w/ National Grid Partners; 42-sensor AEP deployment unlocked ~40% more capacity; National Grid (UK) expanding rollout in 2026

companies.name: Heimdall Power
companies.what: Drone-installed 'magic ball' Neuron sensors clamped onto conductors feeding a DLR software platform.
companies.signal: $25M raise (2024) to scale production; Minnesota co-op deployment showed 63% peak capacity increase

companies.name: Ampacimon
companies.what: Belgian DLR pioneer offering both conductor-vibration sensors and sensorless rating models for TSOs.
companies.signal: DLR project awarded by Svenska kraftnät; deployments across Europe and the Americas; Drone Volt partnership (2025)

companies.name: Gridraven
companies.what: Hardware-free DLR using ML hyperlocal wind forecasting over 3D terrain models — ratings without installing sensors.
companies.signal: €4M raise (Feb 2025, 42CAP + Icebreaker.vc) to expand into the US; claims up to 30% capacity gains

companies.name: Splight
companies.what: ML-based Dynamic Congestion Management that lets fast assets (batteries, data centers) respond to real-time grid conditions, unlocking up to 100% more transfer capacity sensorlessly.
companies.signal: $12.4M raise led by Blue Bear Capital (2025) for US expansion

companies.name: NewGrid

companies.name: Smart Wires
companies.what: Modular power-flow control devices (SSSC) with planning/控 software that push power onto underused lines.

variations.white_space: The constraint is regulatory economics, not physics: US utilities earn returns on capex builds, not on software that defers them, so GET adoption lags Europe; pending FERC incentive/mandate action would unlock the market. Sensorless, software-only DLR (Gridraven, Splight) drops deployment cost and is the natural wedge; topology optimization has exactly one vendor (NewGrid) and is wide open.

companies.name: envelio
